title: FC Dallas 3-0 Portland Timbers: Valiente at the double in Game 1 victory
subtitle: Joaquin Valiente was the star of the show for FC Dallas as they began their MLS Cup campaign with a routine win over the Portland Timbers.
paragraphs: FC Dallas put themselves in a commanding position in their MLS Cup playoff series with the Portland Timbers, as Joaquin Valiente netted twice in their 3-0 victory in Game 1.
Valiente struck twice in the space of two second-half minutes and, despite Portland's late pressure, substitute Sam Sarver added further gloss to the scoreline in the 94th minute.
Dallas claimed just their second win in their last 12 playoff matches since 2018, giving them a 1-0 lead in their Round One best-of-three series ahead of next week's second match.
Petar Musa, the scorer of 13 home goals for Dallas in the regular season, almost gave his team the lead early on, only to see his instinctive effort repelled by James Pantemis.
An end-to-end opening continued as Dallas goalkeeper Daniel was forced to push Ronald Hernandez's bouncing shot behind, before the Brazilian shot-stopper got down low to deny Cole Bassett.
Bassett took aim again from distance, but a fingertip stop from Daniel kept the scores level going into the break, and his saves laid the foundations for Dallas to edge in front.

Moments after seeing his strike smothered from a tight angle by Pantemis, Valiente opened the scoring in the 53rd minute. Daniel Job's effort was parried into the path of the Uruguayan, who volleyed home on the rebound.
Dallas had their second 113 seconds later. Valiente got across Finn Surman at the front post and expertly turned in Job's delivery, with the goal standing after a VAR review.

Valiente squandered a huge chance to complete his hat-trick just before the hour after capitalising on a defensive mistake from Finn Surman, but when faced one-on-one with Pantemis, the Portland goalkeeper stood firm.

The Timbers came within inches of halving the deficit twice late on, with Alexander Aravena's deflected shot hitting the crossbar and the post, before Vincent Janssen failed to turn home from close range after a corner.
Dallas sealed the win in stoppage time at the end of a blistering counter-attack, which saw substitutes Logan Farrington and Sarver combine to cement a huge victory.
Earlier in the day, the New England Revolution took the spoils in their Game 1 clash with the Philadelphia Union, as Marko Mitrovic's side came out on top with a 2-0 triumph.
New England needed just 10 minutes to take the lead when Peyton Miller's strike deflected off Nathan Harriel and wrong-footed Philadelphia goalkeeper Andrew Rick.
The victory was sealed in the 73rd minute by Miller. The American was left unmarked at the back post, and sweetly struck Jack Harrison's teasing cross in off the crossbar.
Valiente piles more away day playoff misery on Portland
Ahead of kick-off, all the talk surrounded Dallas' master marksman in Musa, but it was Valiente – normally the chief creator for Eric Quill's side – who had the clinical touch.

Valiente netted for just the fifth time this season, adding to his 13 assists from the regular season, while he also finished the match with team-high totals for shots (four) and total crosses (four).
There was also an impressive display from Job out on the Dallas left. No player created more chances (four), attempted more dribbles (five) and went into more duels (15) than Job.
Meanwhile, an all-round team display from Dallas inflicted more misery on the road in the postseason for Portland.

The Timbers have now lost five of their last six away playoff matches (W1), a streak that started with their 2018 MLS Cup Final defeat to Atlanta United, and they now know they must make home advantage count at Providence Park next weekend.
Dallas were, however, deserving of their win. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.62 from their 15 attempts to Portland's 1.35 from 12 shots.
